kurz: Egg yolk thickens sauces in two ways: as an [[emulgator|emulsifier]] for fat and water, and by thickening when warmed.
bild_im_kopf: An all-rounder with two talents: go-between for fat and water, and thickener in the warmth.
was_passiert: The lecithin in egg yolk has a water-loving and a fat-loving side and coats fat droplets. Its proteins thicken from about 65 °C and set above about 70 °C.
faustregeln: Never let egg yolk sauces boil.
One yolk carries far more oil than you think: the problem is almost always speed.
